title: German Chocolate Cake with Coconut-Pecan Filling
summary: A three-layer American chocolate cake filled with a caramel-gold coconut and toasted pecan filling, left with its sides bare to show off the layers.
equipment: three 20 cm round cake tins, greased and base-lined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: milk or sweet dark chocolate (about 45% cocoa solids), chopped
fine sea salt or table salt
cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

ingredients.item: large egg whites, at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the coconut-pecan filling
steps.text: Whisk the evaporated milk, brown sugar and egg yolks together in a heavy saucepan, then add the butter and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 12-15 minutes until the mixture thickens, turns a deep caramel colour and reaches 80°C. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla, coconut and pecans, then leave to cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally as it thickens to a spreadable consistency. Making the filling first gives it time to cool and set properly before the cake needs it.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) for at least 20 minutes and grease and base-line the three 20 cm tins. Stir the chopped chocolate into the boiling water until fully melted, then leave to cool.

steps.title: Cream the butter
steps.text: Beat the butter, sugar and salt together for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then the vanilla and the cooled melted chocolate. Beating the butter and sugar well at this stage traps air that helps keep the finished cake light despite its rich filling.

steps.title: Mix in flour and buttermilk
steps.text: Mix in the flour and bicarbonate of soda in three additions, alternating with the buttermilk in two, mixing only until just combined each time. Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them in gently in two additions. Alternating the dry and wet ingredients like this stops the batter from curdling or turning lumpy.

steps.title: Bake the layers
steps.text: Divide the batter between the three tins and bake for 25-30 minutes until the sponges spring back when pressed and a skewer comes out clean. Leave the sponges to settle in their tins for 10 minutes, then tip them out onto a wire rack and let them cool fully before you think about filling.

steps.title: Fill and stack
steps.text: Stack the three layers with a third of the coconut-pecan filling spread between each one and on top, leaving the sides of the cake bare. Leaving the sides unfrosted is traditional for this cake, showing off the layers of filling as you cut into it.

tips: Make the coconut-pecan filling first and let it cool fully - it needs to thicken before it can be spread without running off the layers.
Cook the filling over medium heat, stirring constantly, so the egg yolks thicken smoothly rather than curdling into scrambled flecks.
Alternate the flour and buttermilk in stages rather than adding either all at once, to keep the batter smooth.
Make sure the sponge layers are completely cool before filling, or the warm cake will melt the filling and make it slide.
Leave the sides of the cake bare rather than frosted - it's traditional for this cake and shows off the coconut and toasted pecan filling.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: The filling is made with egg yolks and milk, so keep the cake covered in the fridge and eat within 4 days; take it out 30 minutes before serving so the sponge softens. The unfilled sponge layers can be frozen, well wrapped, for up to 2 months.
